 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal is filed by the Insurance company against the Judgment and award dated 31.03.2022
passed in Mvc No.20/2018 by the Senior Civil Judge and Mact, Chincholi, (for short 'the tribunal')
on the ground of quantum.
2.
The injured claimant aged 23 years working as Mechanic met with accident on 22.03.2016.
He sustained injuries in the accident and took treatment in the Hospital.

He filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking NC: 2025:KHC-K:6609 HC-KAR compensation of Rs.10,90,000/- along with future interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization.
The tribunal considering the entire evidence on record awarded a sum of Rs.3,57,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition.
Being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance company has filed the present appeal on the ground of excess compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance company submitted that, even though the respondent No.2 is served with notice, has remained absent.
The tribunal has erred in taking the disability of the claimant at 7%.
The claimant has sustained fracture of tibial condyle (upper end of left tibia) which is healed.
Hence, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earnings.
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,76,233/- which is excess.
Thus, requested for reduction of the compensation amount.

sentences.text: The claimant sustained fracture of tibial condyle (upper end of left tibia) which is healed.
Ex.P.5 is the wound NC: 2025:KHC-K:6609 HC-KAR certificate.
Ex.P.10 is the discharge summary.
The claimant was hospitalized for five days as per Ex.P.10.
The claimant examined the Doctor as P.W.2 and he assessed the disability at 21% as per disability certificate at Ex.P.7.
He observed that, the claimant has difficulty to walk, climb, sit and squat and there is restriction of left knee movement and the Doctor has assessed the disability at 21%.
The tribunal has taken 1/3rd of 21 which is 7% to the whole body which is correct and reasonable, and needs no interference.
5. Though the petitioner has stated that he was earning a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month, he has not produced any income proof to prove his income.
He met with accident in the year 2016.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his income is to be taken at Rs.8,750/- for the year 2016.
The tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.1,32,300/- towards loss of future income, hence, needs no interference.

6. Learned counsel for the Insurance company submitted that, the medical expenses in a sum of NC:
2025:KHC-K:6609 HC-KAR Rs.1,76,200/- awarded by the tribunal is excess.
On going through the records, it is found that, the claimant has produced medical bills only to an extent of Rs.1,29,200/-.
But the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,76,200/- which is in excess amount of Rs.47,000/-.
The same is reduced to Rs.1,29,200/-.

Hence, the total compensation is as under:
Sl.

No. Heads of compensation Amount 1 Pain and sufferings Rs.20,000/- 2 Attendant charges, food and Rs.1,500/-
conveyance expenses 3 Loss of future income Rs.1,32,300/- 4

Medical expenses Rs.1,29,200/- 5 Loss of income during Rs.17,500/-
treatment 6 Loss of amenities and Rs.10,000/-
nutrition food Total Rs.3,10,500/-
7. The claimant has not filed any appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.
All other heads excluding medical expenses are correct and proper and needs no interference.
